title: COP31 climate summit concludes without final agreement amid fossil fuel rows
seoTitle: COP31 climate summit ends without deal over fossil fuels
dek: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya has concluded without an overarching agreement after nearly 200 nations failed to reach consensus amid disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance.
happened: The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, concluded on 22 November without a final agreement after talks extended two days past their scheduled end. The breakdown occurred after nearly 200 participating countries failed to reach a consensus on the final negotiating text. The primary dispute centred on the absence of explicit references to phasing out fossil fuels in the proposed text. The European Union, United Kingdom, Norway, Panama, Vanuatu, Belize, and the Marshall Islands rejected the draft. Ireland's climate minister, speaking for the EU, stated that the bloc would not endorse a decision failing to mention fossil fuels. Conversely, oil-producing nations opposed explicit phase-out language, arguing that energy transitions must consider economic stability and development needs. The summit also stalled over disagreements on climate finance commitments for developing countries. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and UNFCCC executive secretary Simon Stiell expressed disappointment over the outcome.

sides.says: The EU and countries such as the UK, Norway, Panama, Vanuatu, and the Marshall Islands refused to endorse the text. Ireland's climate minister stated: "We will not endorse a decision [...] that does not even mention fossil fuels", calling a deal without it unconscionable.

India stated that historical emissions have consumed a disproportionate share of the global carbon budget, emphasizing that equity and climate justice must remain central. India also expressed regret that consensus could not be reached on the cover decision.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated he was disappointed that the summit ended without consensus. UNFCCC executive secretary Simon Stiell said that the world cannot afford a repeat of this moment and noted that the process has scope to improve and modernise.

next: Multilateral climate discussions and preparations will continue on the road to COP32 following the collapse of the Antalya agreement.
summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended without a final agreement after nearly 200 nations failed to achieve consensus following two days of overtime negotiations. The breakdown was driven by sharp divisions over the omission of explicit references to phasing out fossil fuels from the text. The European Union and several island nations rejected the draft, while oil-producing economies opposed stringent mitigation language. Disagreements also persisted over financial assistance for vulnerable developing countries.
